correctness.rationale: For a nonalgebraic point x over finite A in H_r, the atomic data are exactly S=N(x)∩A. The one-point extension is K_r-free iff A[S] is K_{r-1}-free, and homogeneity identifies equal neighborhood patterns. This proves the polynomial identity and total type count. #P membership follows from polynomial-time verification of K_{r-1}-freeness for fixed r. The reduction from bipartite #IS via A=B join K_{r-3} has an exact closed offset, and exhaustive replay checked the structural criterion and reduction formula on thousands of finite instances.

value.rationale: The result converts a canonical model-theoretic finite type-space problem into an explicit graph polynomial and locates its exact computational complexity. It shows that even a highly homogeneous free-amalgamation theory can have #P-complete exact finite-parameter type counting, while preserving the full neighborhood-size distribution. The uniform reduction for all fixed Henson K_r-free graphs makes the phenomenon structural rather than a one-off triangle-free coincidence.
